name: .44 Service Revolver
description:
The .44 Service Revolver is the 2200 production designation for the cartridge family descended from the .44 Special — not the Magnum, the Special — a distinction that matters to the people who load it and means nothing to the people who get shot with it. In GLMZ, the .44 SR occupies a narrow but committed market: heavy-frame revolvers carried by people who want maximum caliber diameter with manageable recoil, usually in the outer districts and the Excluded zones where the things you might need to stop are larger than a person. Industrial districts border on wildlife corridors where GLMZ's ecological collapse has produced fauna that does not respect tier designations. A .44 Service Revolver round from a six-inch barrel is not a defensive round — it is a statement of physical authority over a situation.

The .44 SR in its 2200 form is loaded to slightly higher pressure than its ancestor to take advantage of modern case materials and powders, giving it a meaningful velocity improvement without crossing into magnum territory. Slagworks' Irongate line and several small specialty manufacturers produce it in brass-cased configuration almost exclusively — caseless .44 SR has never found a meaningful market because the revolvers that fire it are invariably legacy or near-legacy designs with brass chambers. Modern projectile options exist, including hardcast penetrators for industrial fauna and fragmenting hollow-points for interpersonal defense, but the round's dominant cultural image in GLMZ is a heavy lead slug from a heavy gun in a heavy hand, and that image is accurate.
compatibility_note: Compatible with heavy-frame revolvers chambered for .44 Special or .44 Service Revolver spec. Also compatible with .44 Magnum revolvers, which accept the shorter .44 SR case. Not compatible with semi-automatic platforms without significant modification. Primarily brass-cased; caseless variant is effectively nonexistent in GLMZ production.
reliability_note: Highly reliable. Heavy-caliber revolver cartridge with simple geometry and moderate pressure. Functions in all GLMZ environmental conditions including the unregulated exterior and industrial zones where it is most commonly used. Brass is easy to identify and reload. No energy dependency whatsoever. The combination of revolver mechanical simplicity and proven cartridge dimensions makes this one of the most failure-resistant defensive systems in GLMZ.
